title: Revised 2027 EU ETS1 and initial 2027 EU ETS2 auction calendars published
date_evidence: News article | 1 October 2026 | Directorate-General for Climate Action | 2 min read (visible dateline; a separate Publication date block repeats: 1 October 2026; meta og:updated_time: 2026-10-01T14:00:00+0200)
key_claim: EEX published the first 2027 ETS2 auction calendar: ETS2 auctions start on 18 January 2027 on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, reflecting early auctioning of 2028 volumes, with the 2027 volume including 140 000 000 allowances for the Social Climate Fund and allowances only for member states that have implemented the surrender obligation, with an adjustment to be published later this year.
frame_summary: Presents the ETS2 auction start as implementation proceeding on schedule, while conceding the 2027 volumes are provisional because several member states have not yet implemented the surrender obligation and penalties.
verbatim_quote: will take place on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, starting on 7 January and 18 January respectively.
verbatim_list: Yesterday, the European Energy Exchange (EEX) published the revised 2027 EU ETS1 and the new 2027 EU ETS2 auction calendars.
The first published calendar for ETS2 allowances reflects the early auctioning of 2028 volumes
Auctions of ETS2 allowances will start at 1pm and end at 3pm.
Pursuant to Article 13(7) of the Auctioning Regulation, the current auction volume for 2027 includes 140 000 000 allowances
notes: Canonical primary notice fixing the auction start date and mechanics; the Key source for the scan. The volume-adjustment sentence is the evidence for uneven member-state implementation.

title: Drittes Gesetz zur Aenderung des Brennstoffemissionshandelsgesetzes (CO2-Preis soll 2027 stabil gehalten werden)
date_evidence: meta-date: 24.09.2026 (article dateline: (sas/hau/24.09.2026); body: Der Bundestag hat am Donnerstag, 24. September 2026, in erster Lesung ...)
key_claim: The government bill holds Germany's national fuel-emissions-trading CO2 price for 2027 in a corridor of 55 to 65 euros per tonne, unchanged from 2026, as a bridge year before the EU ETS2 brings a European market price from 2028; the Bundestag passed the bill on 15 October 2026.
frame_summary: Frames the frozen 2027 corridor as planning certainty and relief for companies and consumers in a transition year created by the ETS2 postponement to 2028.
verbatim_quote: in einem Preiskorridor von 55 bis 65 Euro liegen.
verbatim_list: Hintergrund der Reform ist die Verschiebung des neuen europäischen Emissionshandels für Gebäude und Verkehr
Donnerstag, 15. Oktober 2026
notes: Tier 1 primary source in German (multi-language pass). The page is the Bundestag's rolling record of the bill: first reading 24 September 2026, hearing 7 October, final passage 15 October 2026.

title: Outcome of the European Council meeting of 15-16 October 2026 (Post-European Council Briefing)
date_evidence: Last updated: 20 October 2026 (visible dateline on the briefing page; og:url path contains /EPRS/2026/10/)
key_claim: At the 15-16 October 2026 European Council six member states (the Visegrad Four, Italy and Greece) called for postponing ETS2 and Estonia for scrapping it, but no further postponement was granted; leaders asked the Commission to update the assessment of all impacts of ETS2, in particular its design and safeguards, and asked co-legislators to accelerate the market stability reserve legislation.
frame_summary: Frames the October summit as the sceptics contained: a lengthy ETS discussion ended with an impact reassessment and faster market-stability-reserve work rather than any new delay, with a Nordic-led camp backed by Germany, Spain, France, Portugal and the Netherlands holding the line.
verbatim_quote: Considering the fact that ETS2 had already been postponed from 2027 to 2028, no further postponement was granted.
verbatim_list: A lengthy discussion took place on the EU emissions trading system (ETS) and the upcoming ETS2 for transport and buildings.
to update the assessment of all impacts of ETS2, in particular its design and safeguards
(the Visegrád Four – Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia – Italy and Greece) called for the postponement of ETS2
to accelerate the ongoing legislative process on the market stability reserve to curb excessive price volatility
Germany, Spain, France, Portugal and the Netherlands also supported the Nordic view.
notes: The page shows only a Last updated date (20 October 2026); Post-European Council Briefings are one-off publications issued days after the summit, so this is treated as the publication date. The briefing quotes the Council conclusions' ETS2 wording directly; consilium.europa.eu itself refuses automated fetches.

title: Early auction: ETS2 auctions to start 18 January 2027 (ETS2 auction volumes: 293.2m EUA2s in 2027)
key_claim: The 2027 ETS2 auction calendar schedules 293.2 million allowances for auction, front-loaded at the start of the year, with early auctions starting Monday 18 January 2027.
frame_summary: Reads the calendar as the market's first clear view of early EUA2 supply ahead of ETS2's 2028 launch, emphasising the front-loading of volumes.
verbatim_quote: With 293.2 million allowances scheduled for auction and volumes front-loaded at the start of the year
verbatim_list: Today the European Commission and EEX published the ETS2 auction volumes for 2027.
The 2027 ETS2 auction calendar is now published, giving the market its first clear view of early EUA2 supply.
notes: Analysis section of the article sits behind a demo gate; the figures used are in the open text and metadata. By Ingvild Sorhus, Veyt European Carbon.

title: Council must take position on ETS this year, or risk ETS2 delay
key_claim: A further ETS2 delay is not Veyt's base case, but the risk rises sharply if the ETS Directive review is still open when Spanish and French elections change the Council arithmetic; Poland, Czechia, Italy and others keep calling for a further delay while early auctions are two months away.
frame_summary: Argues the 2028 start holds in the base case, with the ETS Directive review, Council arithmetic after Spanish and French elections, and national transposition gaps as the routes a further delay could still take.
verbatim_quote: The start of early auctions of ETS2 allowances is two months away, yet Poland, Czechia, Italy, and others have continued to challenge the system, repeatedly calling for a further delay.
verbatim_list: The main arena for that fight is the ETS Directive review, which focuses on ETS1 and does not envisage reopening ETS2
whether the review is settled before elections in Spain and France change the Council arithmetic
notes: Primary sourced counter-evidence for the Counter-Argument. By Florian Baier and Anders Nordeng; body partly behind a demo gate, quotes are from the open text.

title: €100,000 more for diesel? Why ETS2 may not hit Irish hauliers quite as expected
date_evidence: Pölös Zsófia Journalist Trans.info | 1.09.2026 (visible byline; the site writes dates dd.mm.yyyy)
key_claim: Ireland is pursuing an ETS2 derogation under which regulated fuel suppliers are exempt from surrendering allowances for 2027 to 2030, provided the national carbon tax paid exceeds the average ETS2 auction clearing price; an illustrative 10 cents per litre carbon increase adds 100,000 euros to the annual fuel bill of a fleet using one million litres.
frame_summary: Argues ETS2's cost for Irish hauliers is contingent on national policy choices, with the derogation, the carbon tax and the diesel rebate scheme standing between the EU price and the pump.
verbatim_quote: A carbon-related increase of just 10 cents per litre would add €100,000 to the annual fuel bill
verbatim_list: the carbon tax actually paid by the regulated entity must be higher than the average ETS2 auction clearing price
The derogation can operate for the years 2027 to 2030.
is now due to become fully operational in 2028
ETS2 allowance auctions are nevertheless scheduled to begin in January 2027.
notes: The 10 cents per litre scenario is attributed by the article to HGV Ireland as illustrative rather than a forecast; the body presents it as an illustration. The one-million-litre fleet framing is the article's own.

title: Commission 'has grasped' need to postpone ETS2, Christodoulides says
date_evidence: meta-article:published_time: 2026-10-16T13:49:40.000Z (visible: Cyprus News Friday 16 October | 16:49, By Tom Cleaver)
key_claim: Cyprus's president said after the October 2026 summit that the Commission 'has grasped' the need to suspend ETS2 beyond 2028, with Cyprus one of seven countries supporting suspension; Czech PM Babis warned 'if you want ETS2 I guarantee you will lose elections'.
frame_summary: Frames the postponement push as politically alive at head-of-state level even after the summit, with Christodoulides claiming the Commission privately accepts suspension beyond 2028.
verbatim_quote: Cyprus is one of seven countries which has supported suspending the implementation of ETS2
verbatim_list: if you want ETS2 I guarantee you will lose elections
notes: The seven-country count includes Cyprus and differs from EPRS's six-state count of those who raised postponement at the summit table; the body uses the EPRS framing and this source for the head-of-state push. Counter-evidence for the Counter-Argument.
